chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Generosity is more prompting to good than regard for kinship.

key_terms.أَعْطَفُ: More prompting, more inclined, or more effective in drawing near
key_terms.الرَّحِمِ: Kinship, family ties, or the womb

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between generosity and kinship in prompting virtue according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this famous aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contrasts the voluntary, active nature of generosity (karam) with the inherent, passive bond of kinship (rahim). Shia scholars often interpret 'more bent' (a'atifu) as indicating that generosity actively draws hearts closer through conscious benevolence, whereas kinship relies on natural affinity. This highlights the superior motivational power of giving and benevolence over mere familial ties.
